concepts.learning_objective: Classify economic activities into primary, secondary and tertiary sectors by the nature of the activity.
Explain how the three sectors depend on one another using everyday examples.

topics.title: Comparing the three sectors: GDP and historical change
topics.ncert_sections: Comparing the Three Sectors; Historical Change in Sectors

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish final goods from intermediate goods and explain why only final goods are counted.
Define GDP and calculate the value of production while avoiding double counting.
Describe how the most important sector changed over time in now developed countries.

topics.title: Primary, secondary and tertiary sectors in India
topics.ncert_sections: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Sectors in India

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the reasons for the rising importance of the tertiary sector in India's production.
Analyse why employment did not shift out of the primary sector as production did.
Explain underemployment or disguised unemployment with rural and urban examples.
Suggest ways of creating employment through irrigation, credit, agro-based industry and services.
Describe the provisions and purpose of MGNREGA 2005 as the Right to Work.

topics.title: Organised and unorganised sectors
topics.ncert_sections: Division of Sectors as Organised and Unorganised; How to Protect Workers in the Unorganised Sector?

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between the organised and unorganised sectors on the basis of employment conditions.
Identify vulnerable workers in the unorganised sector and explain why they need protection.

topics.title: Sectors in terms of ownership: public and private
topics.ncert_sections: Sectors in Terms of Ownership: Public and Private Sectors

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between public and private sectors on the basis of ownership and motive.
Explain why the government undertakes or supports certain economic activities.
